findings.location: lines 90-127: plane profile and dynamin collar update
findings.evidence: The collar is fixed at world y=0.65 and has radius 0.22 before scalar constriction. At p=0.30 the actual rendered membrane midplane has radius 0.695274 there, whereas the complete conservative collar radial extent is only 0.273; at p=0.34 these values are 0.422926 and 0.273. The collar therefore occupies the extracellular pit lumen instead of wrapping the cytosolic neck. At p=0.39..0.429999 every membrane vertex is identical while collar center radius changes from 0.134067 to 0.072600. The collar also stays visible until .44 despite scission at .43. Measurements are in evidence/traffic/diagnostic.json.
findings.whyWrong: The scene says dynamin constricts the membrane neck, but places it inside the invagination and independently shrinks it through an unchanged membrane. This reverses the relevant membrane sidedness and depicts constriction without membrane constriction.
findings.fix: Drive the actual connected membrane neck and the cytosolic dynamin collar from one constriction state. Derive collar anchors/radius from the actual neck surface with outward clearance; recruit only at that physical neck and remove/disassemble coherently at scission. Preserve the open-to-sealed cargo topology and a smooth membrane continuation to the detached carrier.
findings.verification: Across recruitment, every constriction sample and scission-adjacent frames, measure collar vertices against the actual membrane surface/neck cross-sections, verify cytosolic placement and coupled decreasing membrane/collar radius, and reject the original p=.30/.34 luminal position and unchanged .39..43 membrane. Check bound cargo and receptor sidedness during any neck-profile repair.

findings: Confirmed independent collar shrinkage and membrane-side failure under 20261004-traffic-01.
Inspected .12/.29/.43/.44/.45/.49/.54/.65/.67/.73/.76/.9/.96 switches/eases, with stage-adjacent numeric samples.

findings.kind: continuous playback and persistent membrane attachments
findings.location: lines 186-219: pump and glycan pre/post-fusion parameterization
findings.evidence: Across p=.65-1e-8 to p=.65 the same visible glycan group jumps by up to 2.369646 world units, while the V-ATPase jumps 0.892791. The pre-fusion sphere parameter t is reused directly on the entire merged envelope, so membrane-bound actors on the lysosome abruptly reappear across the former autophagosome region. This is a finite jump at a fixed threshold, not fast but continuous movement. Before/after coordinates are retained in evidence/traffic/diagnostic.json.
findings.whyWrong: These actors are continuously visible attached membrane structures. An arbitrary change of surface parameterization cannot physically move them across the organelle at fusion, and creates a large playback discontinuity even as the surrounding profile is subsequently interpolated smoothly.
findings.fix: Preserve every lysosomal membrane actor world anchor at the fusion threshold, map each to the corresponding right-lobe coordinate of the common envelope and then move it continuously on the changing rendered surface. Derive orientation from the same surface as needed. Review the small pre-fusion envelope gap and nascent neck while checking the fusion frame, without reducing detail.
findings.verification: A regression must compare actual world transforms at .65-epsilon, .65 and .65+epsilon and bound displacement in proportion to the interval; verify each glycan base and pump membrane rotor remains anchored throughout fusion and rounding. The original 2.370/.893 jumps must fail.

findings: At fusion the pre-fusion spherical midplanes have a .18 gap; the immediate common envelope differs from the previous sphere union by up to .110173 at sampled profile points. Retained for root rendered review; no separate scientific verdict inferred solely from this discrete topology change.
Inspected .44/.47/.63/.65/.71/.73/.8/.82/.9/.96/.995 visibility and interpolation boundaries; fragment appearance and final aggregate disappearance are schematic hydrolysis transitions.
limits: No browser/rendered fusion review or frame-rate acceptance performed.
Per-enzyme catalytic docking and actual cleavage sites are not modeled; reference folds support molecular identity rather than reaction dynamics.

limitations: Membrane sources, upstream signaling, fusion machinery and returned metabolites are explicitly outside the scene.
Inner-membrane removal is a topology-preserving schematic timing choice, not a claim of an experimentally measured uniform polar erosion trajectory.
Native protein backbone references were checked against depositor identity; all original CIF coordinate values were not redownloaded/rehashed in this audit.
